title: A Small Lead Becomes a Win

scenes.tts: A target makes nerve growth factor, called N G F, but too little for every sympathetic neuron that reaches it. So which neurons get to live? Share it evenly, and they all live or all die together. If the first axon took everything, nothing would explain how a neuron receiving some N G F could fall behind. Something else must pick the winners.
scenes.caption: A target makes nerve growth factor, called NGF, but too little for every sympathetic neuron that reaches it. So which neurons get to live? Share it evenly, and they all live or all die together. If the first axon took everything, nothing would explain how a neuron receiving some NGF could fall behind. Something else must pick the winners.
scenes.visual: A ring of neurons reach for a target holding a few NGF dots; question mark; an even share turns all neurons green then all red; a first-axon-takes-all case leaves no way to fall behind.
scenes.narration: A target makes nerve growth factor, called NGF, but too little for every sympathetic neuron that reaches it. So which neurons get to live? Share it evenly, and they all live or all die together. If the first axon took everything, nothing would explain how a neuron receiving some NGF could fall behind. Something else must pick the winners.

scenes.tts: In mouse sympathetic neurons, N G F raises its own receptor, T R K A. With N G F, T R K A rises, and without it, T R K A falls. So a neuron with a little more T R K A collects more N G F. It makes still more T R K A and pulls further ahead. That loop is positive feedback, but the model also needed longer N G F signals.
scenes.caption: In mouse sympathetic neurons, NGF raises its own receptor, TrkA. With NGF, TrkA rises, and without it, TrkA falls. So a neuron with a little more TrkA collects more NGF. It makes still more TrkA and pulls further ahead. That loop is positive feedback, but the model also needed longer NGF signals.
scenes.visual: Two neurons with TrkA bars: NGF arrives and the bar rises, absent NGF it falls; a loop of arrows between more TrkA and more NGF collected while one bar pulls away.
scenes.narration: In mouse sympathetic neurons, NGF raises its own receptor, TrkA. With NGF, TrkA rises, and without it, TrkA falls. So a neuron with a little more TrkA collects more NGF. It makes still more TrkA and pulls further ahead. That loop is positive feedback, but the model also needed longer NGF signals.

scenes.tts: In simulations with steady N G F production, feedback on both T R K A level and signal duration split the neurons into winners and losers. A young neuron is naive and responds poorly to N G F. Enough N G F carries it over a threshold, which is sensitization. It raises T R K A, and that is a competitive advantage. Winning the supply is selection, and neighbours that stayed behind lose.
scenes.caption: In simulations with steady NGF production, feedback on both TrkA level and signal duration split the neurons into winners and losers. A young neuron is naive and responds poorly to NGF. Enough NGF carries it over a threshold, which is sensitization. It raises TrkA, and that is a competitive advantage. Winning the supply is selection, and neighbours that stayed behind lose.
scenes.visual: TrkA against time for ten neurons that start nearly equal and split into green winners and red losers; a dot replays one winner through four stage chips.
scenes.narration: In simulations with steady NGF production, feedback on both TrkA level and signal duration split the neurons into winners and losers. A young neuron is naive and responds poorly to NGF. Enough NGF carries it over a threshold, which is sensitization. It raises TrkA, and that is a competitive advantage. scenes.tts: Winners do more than pull ahead. Strongly supported neurons make B D N F and N T four. These act through p seventy five on weakly supported neighbours. In this setting, p seventy five can promote death. A neuron rich in T R K A is protected, and a neuron poor in T R K A is not.
scenes.caption: Winners do more than pull ahead. Strongly supported neurons make BDNF and NT-4. These act through p75 on weakly supported neighbours. In this setting, p75 can promote death. A neuron rich in TrkA is protected, and a neuron poor in TrkA is not.
scenes.visual: A strong neuron with a tall TrkA bar sends BDNF and NT-4 across to a weak neuron with a short bar; the p75 receptor on the weak neuron receives it and it turns red; a shield rings the strong one.
scenes.narration: Winners do more than pull ahead. Strongly supported neurons make BDNF and NT-4. These act through p75 on weakly supported neighbours. In this setting, p75 can promote death. A neuron rich in TrkA is protected, and a neuron poor in TrkA is not.

scenes.tts: Does punishment matter? In simulations, it made the split faster, because weak neurons lingered without it. In mice lacking p seventy five, the loss is delayed but not prevented. In the lab's own study, neuron number falls more slowly and reaches the control level. The losers still die, because they lack enough N G F.

scenes.visual: Neuron number against age: a steep curve and a shallower curve reach the same level; tags change from simulation to mouse.
scenes.narration: Does punishment matter? In simulations, it made the split faster, because weak neurons lingered without it. In mice lacking p75, the loss is delayed but not prevented. scenes.tts: So a limited supply does not pick the winners alone. A small early lead boosts T R K A and signal length. Winners punish weak neighbours through p seventy five, and the split comes faster. All this comes from one cell type, the sympathetic neuron, in mice and rat cultures. Remember the rule: feedback turns a small lead into survival, and punishment speeds it up.
